neighbours.label: the infinitive marker 'to' after a passive or necessity verb in technical prose ('is allowed to', 'was used to', 'has to be'); prepositional 'to' and casual infinitives stay quiet
fire: After mixing, the epoxy is allowed to harden at room temperature for a day.
Thin films of gold have been used to coat the electrodes in many sensors.
In this design the filter has to be replaced after every hundred cycles.
The cells were left to recover in fresh medium before the second treatment.
A small vacuum pump is used to remove air bubbles from the resin.
Each sample must be allowed to settle before the absorbance is read.
Magnetic beads were used to separate the labelled proteins from the lysate.
The membrane is then permitted to dry slowly in a covered dish.
quiet: After mixing, the epoxy is moved to a shelf at room temperature for a day.
Thin films of gold have been added to the electrodes in many sensors.
In this design the filter is attached to the pump with two clamps.
The cells were returned to fresh medium before the second treatment.
A small vacuum pump is connected to the chamber by a rubber hose.
Each sample is transferred to a clean tube before the absorbance is read.
Magnetic beads were added to the lysate together with the labelled proteins.
The membrane is then sent to the imaging room in a covered dish.

predictions: fire 0.2-0.6 on ' to' before a verb in technical/procedural passives; prepositional ' to' in the same register below 0.05
notes: Card: ' to' x17 of top 32, after 'ability', 'allowed', 'used', 'appear', in scientific prose; also ' can', ' be', ' is' before verbs. Probe: 'is allowed to cure' 0.521, 'have been used to etch' 0.281, 'has to be cleared' 0.227, 'ability to cleave' 0.115, 'can fly' 0.123; prepositional 'sent to the laboratory' 0.007, 'drove to the coast' 0.002; casual 'want to go home' 0.029.
